beal-opera-8-5-mm: Liked as a thin, light rope for multipitch and ice; a few find the sheath fuzzes easily.
black-diamond-aspect-pro: Praised for comfort and a supportive feel on crack and multipitch; a couple report delamination.
black-diamond-atc-pilot: Loved for smooth feeding and lowering and good value; a few note slippage with some ropes.
black-diamond-solution-guide-harness: Liked as comfortable and roomy enough for a big trad rack; a couple saw it wear out in two years.
black-diamond-solution-harness: Praised for wide, very comfortable leg loops; many find the fixed loops hard to size.
butora-gomi: Liked as comfortable and sticky with good heel and toe hooks; some find the toes cramped.
butora-rubicon: Praised for very comfortable fit and good smearing on slab; one says it is poor on steep overhangs.
edelrid-autana: Valued for adjustable leg loops and thick padding for big thighs; two found the gear loops tiny.
edelrid-giga-jul: Known for covering assisted braking, guide mode and rappels in one; many find feeding rope draggy.
edelrid-mega-jul: Liked as light, simple and durable for single-pitch belaying; many find guide mode hard work.
edelrid-ohm: Valued for helping a lot when belaying a much heavier climber; several disliked the hard catches.
edelrid-ohmega: Praised for belaying a much heavier climber more smoothly than the Ohm; some found the settings fiddly.
edelrid-pinch: Liked for smooth belaying and clipping straight to the belay loop; some find thick ropes draggy.
evolv-defy-lace: Liked as a comfortable, good-value shoe that is not too aggressive; one found the toes painful.
evolv-kira: Loved as very comfortable and long lasting for all-day wear; some find it too soft for micro edges.
evolv-kronos: Praised as comfortable and long-lasting, especially on wide feet; some find the heel baggy.
la-sportiva-kubo: Liked as comfortable once broken in; many report a painful first few sessions.
la-sportiva-skwama: Loved for a roomy toe box and good heel hooks; many find it wears out within months.
misty-mountain-cadillac: Praised as plush, very comfortable and durable for trad and big walls; climbers say it is heavy.
organic-big-pad: Known for being large, stiff and very durable; many find it heavy and bulky to carry.
petzl-aquila: Loved for five gear loops and adjustable leg loops on trad and sport; one finds it pinchy.
petzl-corax: Praised as comfortable and very adjustable for big hips or thighs; some find it uncomfortable hanging.
petzl-luna: Loved for comfort with a small waist and big thighs; a few found it bulky or tight at the legs.
petzl-neox: Loved for smooth rope pay-out on lead, close to a tube device; many find it locks on thick ropes.
petzl-selena: Liked as comfortable for sport and gym, even on wider thighs; a few found the leg loops loose.
petzl-sitta: Valued as light and small to pack, with room for much of a trad rack; one found hanging uncomfortable.
scarpa-drago: Loved for a soft, sensitive feel and sticky rubber; many find holes appear at the toes within months.
scarpa-drago-lv: Praised for a soft feel and snug heel on low-volume feet; many report a painful break-in.
scarpa-helix: Liked as a comfortable, good-value, long-lasting lace-up; some find it limited on tiny holds.
scarpa-instinct-vsr: Valued as a versatile all-rounder with good edging; many describe a painful break-in.
scarpa-instinct-vsr-lv: Loved for a snug heel that suits narrow heels; some have a tough break-in.
scarpa-veloce: Loved for being soft, sticky and comfortable on wide feet; many find it wears out within months.
scarpa-veloce-l: Praised for very sticky rubber and comfort on wide feet; several find the heel bags out.
tenaya-indalo: Liked for comfort and good edging for a performance shoe; many have to size well below street size.
tenaya-mastia: Loved as very comfortable on wide feet or low-volume heels; a few find the toes tight.
